description:
About the Position

This Earlham Institute PhD uses genomic diversity to support celery breeding against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. apii race 4. The project involves collaboration with Tozer Seeds. This PhD opening at Earlham Institute centres on Celery Pangenomics and Disease Resistance at Earlham Institute, UK. Disciplinary scope: Biology, Bioinformatics. Location: Norwich, United Kingdom. Full funding is provided; financial support is listed as £21,805/year. The stated deadline is 30 November 2026.

Official Project Title

Future-proofing celery with genomics, pangenomics and AI-assisted gene discovery

Research Focus and Methods

Analyse diverse celery material, link field resistance with SNP, k-mer, haplotype and pangenome variation, and use time-course RNA sequencing to compare defence responses. Later work can explore candidate genes through comparative genomics and AI-assisted prioritisation.

Research Training and Development

Develop bioinformatics, statistical analysis and industry-facing research skills.

Funding and Duration

Studentship funding and award conditions
ComponentDetails
AwardPhD studentship; selection is competitive
ProgrammeBBSRC Norwich Research Park Biosciences DTP
DurationFour years
StipendUKRI-rate living stipend. The programme quotes £21,805 per year for 2026/27; the 2027/28 rate is not yet published on the checked funding page.
Tuition and research supportFour-year NRPDTP award: tuition, living stipend and research funding.
Award conditionsSelection is competitive; an advertised project does not guarantee a studentship.
Research Training Support Grant£5,000 per year
Visa and IHS contributionFor October 2027 entrants, up to £3,500 towards eligible individual visa and immigration health surcharge costs after enrolment and registration, with evidence. Dependants are excluded.
Stipend amount status£21,805 is the published 2026/27 reference rate. Subsequent academic-year rates and the amount in an individual funding offer should be checked separately.

Eligibility and English Language

Applicant qualifications and funding eligibility
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityUK and international applicants; international recruitment is capped at 30% of the programme intake.
Academic preparationFirst or upper-second-class honours degree, or equivalent; alternative experience routes are described in the programme rules.
Project interests and skillsInterest in crop genomics, plant pathology and breeding.
English languageUEA English-language requirements apply. Accepted evidence or an applicable exemption is required; the requirement may be met as an offer condition.
Alternative academic routeA lower-second-class degree may be considered with a suitable master’s qualification or significant relevant research or non-academic experience.

About Earlham Institute

Earlham Institute is a life sciences research institute based at Norwich Research Park in England. Its research focuses on genomics and computational biology, using experimental and analytical approaches to understand living systems. The institute supports scientific collaboration, specialist technology and researcher training, connecting biological data with questions across diverse organisms.

Official website: https://www.earlham.ac.uk/

Application Dates and Location

Deadline, start date and research location

Research locationNorwich, United Kingdom

Contact

  • Email: jose.devega@earlham.ac.uk
  • Email: anthony.hall@earlham.ac.uk

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 30 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  1. Read the official project advert and NRPDTP eligibility guidance.
  2. Discuss the project with the supervisor; the programme strongly encourages contact before applying.
  3. Complete the mandatory NRPDTP Personal Statement and Research Statement proformas; missing proformas result in rejection.
  4. Prepare your CV, academic records, two referee contacts and any required English-language or identity documents.
  5. Submit through UEA’s admissions system using the link on the official NRPDTP guidance page.

You may apply for up to three NRPDTP projects, with a separate application for each.

Application Checklist

  • NRPDTP Personal Statement Proforma
  • NRPDTP Research Statement Proforma
  • CV
  • Academic certificates and transcripts, including current results for unfinished degrees
  • At least two referee contacts, including one academic referee
  • English-language evidence, where required
  • Passport and relevant immigration documents, where required
